title: Katie Taylor cruises past Flora Pili in farewell fight before packed Croke Park
content:
Katie Taylor took a solo lap around the ring Saturday night at Croke Park in Dublin, soaking in the adoration of the more than 80,000 fans who had just watched the Irish sporting icon win her farewell fight over IBO super lightweight champion Flora Pili via unanimous decision.

The 40-year-old Taylor, who had said throughout the buildup to Saturday’s bout that she planned to retire after the fight, took her time as she circled the ring one last time, waving to the crowd and blowing kisses along the way. After she visited all four corners, she laid down her gloves in the center of the ring to mark the end of her career, for which she’ll be remembered as one of the top fighters of her era and one of the greatest female boxers of all time.

With the win over Pili, Taylor improved her professional record to 26-1 and became the undisputed 140-pound world champion for the second time in her career. Taylor controlled the action throughout, overwhelming Pili with the multiple-punch combinations and in-and-out footwork that have been hallmarks of Taylor’s fighting style since her days as an amateur standout representing Ireland at the 2012 and 2016 Olympics. Two judges scored the bout 100-90, and the third had it 98-91, all for Taylor.

“We did it — we brought boxing back to Croke Park,” Taylor told the crowd during her postfight interview. The last time the famed Irish venue hosted boxing was July 19, 1972, when Muhammad Ali defeated Alvin Lewis there.

“You were with me in London 2012; you were with me with the heartbreak of Rio. You stayed with me when I turned pro,” Taylor told the crowd. “You stayed with me, traveled around the world with me. And now you are here with me, and it’s amazing. I don’t know any other country that would sell 80,000 tickets. Ireland is the only country.”

Few fighters get the send-off they spend a career dreaming of. But then, not many have the lasting impact on the sport that Taylor has. She retires as a three-time undisputed champion (once at lightweight and twice at super lightweight), a five-time world amateur champion, an Olympic gold medalist and the fighter who showed that, given the right backing and platform, women’s boxing can be everything men’s boxing can — and sometimes more.

From the moment she turned professional in 2016, Taylor dreamed of fighting in Ireland. It took some time, though. She fought in the biggest stadiums and arenas in England, Wales and the U.S. before finally realizing that goal with a bout against Chantelle Cameron at the 3Arena in Dublin in her 23rd fight.

Croke Park was always the dream, though. Given Taylor had already achieved so many others, it was no surprise that she ticked that one off, too.

“Over the last 10 years, I don’t even think I had the capacity to dream these things,” she told The Athletic before her farewell fight. “What’s happened over these last 10 years — headlining Madison Square Garden on a couple of occasions, being on the same card as Mike Tyson, having a chance to headline the 3Arena — has been fantastic. Now to have a fight in Croke Park — the last person to have fought there is obviously Muhammad Ali, so to follow in his footsteps, this is crazy. This is wild.”

The fight was shown live on free-to-air television in Ireland (as well as globally on streaming platform DAZN), and sections of the sellout crowd where alcohol was not permitted were reserved for families. It was as big as it gets in boxing, and it offered a glimpse of the impact Taylor has had on her home nation and beyond.

“She’s just a great fighter — one of the best athletes to ever do it,” a boy interviewed on RTE at the open workout earlier this week said. “Best Irish athlete ever, probably.”
